summary: A comedian couple as guests, and the thread is mostly delight at how naturally funny they are with almost no criticism. The most valuable comment in the set is from a long-time viewer who lists a format element the show has quietly dropped — staged role-play situations where guests act out how they actually flirt or make up after a fight, rather than just describing it — and argues it was what made the show unlike anything else. Another cluster is guest requests, including a specific ask for an episode 100 featuring all three hosts' real partners, plus names from the comedian circuit. Viewers also notice and enjoy the product tie-in being folded into the guest's own dialogue rather than read out, and a separate thread observes that the guest's wife has become a performer in her own right through these appearances.

audience_signals: Long-tenure viewers track format drift and can name exactly which segment was dropped — the staged role-play scenarios — and want it back; that is a free content-development note from the people who watch every episode
Tie-in copy delivered inside guest dialogue reads as a joke to be enjoyed rather than an interruption, which is the sponsor pattern this audience accepts
Milestone episodes are anticipated in advance and viewers propose the concept themselves
Comedian guests produce high satisfaction at low production cost — no staging, no location, and the humour carries the episode
Recurring guests build their own following on the channel, which creates a bench of semi-regulars
content_requests: Bring back staged role-play situations with guests
An episode 100 with all three hosts' real partners
